Title: 'Criticising PM is not a crime': Anwar assures students
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: No student will be prosecuted for expressing their views, even if they criticise the prime minister, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Speaking to local and international students at iFUTURE 2026 at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur today, Anwar said young people must act as society's conscience against corruption and injustice.
"No one will be prosecuted just because of their ideas and their criticism, including if the student leader chooses to criticise the Prime Minister.
"That is not a crime.
"You have to defend your position, but it's not a crime to criticise the policies of this government," he said.
Anwar said he had asked Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, his deputy Adam Adli Abd Halim and the ministry to take immediate action against provisions in the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 that could be seen as restricting student freedoms and activities.
"That is what I mean by amending or scrapping those provisions which can be perceived and be abused," he said.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/08/1511577/anwar-announces-abolition-universities-and-university-colleges-act
In August, Anwar announced that the government would abolish the Act following concerns raised by university students.
Anwar said he had long questioned the notion that young people were merely leaders of the future.
"What makes you think that the young are not leaders on their own right now?
"You represent the present and the future. You must represent the conscience of the present. The present society cannot condone corruption, cannot condone exploitation, cannot condone and accept injustice," he said.
He added that students, like their elders, would make mistakes and that teachers and parents had a duty to advise and correct them.
"But similarly, so are the leaders. Leaders sometimes commit blunders. Look at history, recent history of our country. Look at the various scandals, billions lost," he said.
Anwar said Malaysia was among the few countries to rank education as its largest budget allocation, followed by healthcare.
He also said he took a strong stance against racism and religious bigotry, adding that the country's problems were not rooted in race or religion.
"It's the crooks who use race and religion to hide their own excesses," he said.
He said every community deserved to have its rights defended.
"The Malays, the Chinese, the Indians, the Ibans, the Kadazans, they are all my children and they deserve to be given the right and protection," he said.
Anwar urged participants to share suggestions with the government if they identified weaknesses during the programme.
"If you have any suggestions, please share with us so that we can work together to help one another," he said.
"We want you to feel that Malaysia is also your home, your second home," he told international participants.

Title: Anwar: All government contracts to be fully transparent from 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All government contracts will be made fully transparent from next year, with the public able to access details of successful contractors, contract values and project progress, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar said the measure would cover all public projects and allow communities to assess whether developments in their areas were being carried out by responsible contractors.
"I said from next year, every single contract, building schools or hospitals or universities or roads, must be fully transparent.
"Who wins the contract, what's the amount, which company gets the contract, what's the cost, what's the progress, and why this company won against other competitors.
"That is going to be very transparent, everybody can read and see," he said in his speech at iFUTURE 2026 at Dewan Merdeka, World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, today.
Also present was Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
When tabling the 2027 Budget on Friday, Anwar said the government would
disclose project details
, including contractors' names and contract values, once the Government Procurement Act comes into force in 2027.
Citing a new secondary school in Tumpat as an example, he said residents should have access to full details of projects being built in their areas.
"We want to make sure that people of Tumpat would know precisely what's the cost of that school, what's the cost of the land, who the contractor is, what's the progress of the project.
"Let the people of Tumpat then see for themselves if the school is being built by responsible contractors or not. This is going to be the new Malaysia I'm talking about," he said.
Anwar said the government had been able to increase spending on education, healthcare, gig workers and young graduates by addressing leakages.
"Because we start with governance, with good governance. Stop these leakages, and ensure that contracts are done transparently," he said.
He added that the government had raised the minimum wage three times in the nearly four years since he became prime minister.
Anwar also said billions of ringgit lost in past scandals should instead have been channelled into education.
"Billions lost. And that money was supposed to be spent on the students, on our schools, on our universities, not to be stolen by those corrupt people," he said.
He also criticised those who, he said, invoked race and religion to deflect attention from wrongdoing.
"You choose to squander billions on your family account, and when this is exposed, you talk about Malay survival and Islam," he said.

Title: Viral crash: Suspects led cops on chase from Bukit Antarabangsa to Setiawangsa
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two men were arrested after a police pursuit from Jalan Wangsa 5 in Bukit Antarabangsa ended in a crash at the Jalan Jelatek traffic light intersection in Setiawangsa today.
The suspects, who were in an Isuzu D-Max pickup truck, were found with equipment believed to be for cable theft.
City Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said preliminary investigations found that the pickup truck's driver, 32, and his 21-year-old passenger had attempted to flee a police inspection.
The chase ended when the driver allegedly lost control and rammed into a Proton Wira, a Proton Persona and a Toyota Harrier at the intersection.
No injuries were reported.
Mohd Zamzuri said Ampang Jaya police made the arrests.
Video footage of the chase and crash went viral on social media, with many likening it to a scene from the
Grand Theft Auto
video game series.
The case is being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code, Section 108 of the Road Transport Act 1987, Sections 427 and 431A of the Penal Code, and Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
The offences cover obstructing public servants from discharging their duties, the use of fraudulent vehicle registration numbers or road tax, destruction of property, as well as reckless and dangerous driving.
Meanwhile, Ampang Jaya police chief, Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid, said an inspection of the vehicle uncovered several items, including a parang, a sickle and equipment suspected to have been used for cable theft, including a manhole cover opener.
"Police also seized substances suspected to be drugs from both suspects for further investigation," he told the press today.
Earlier, several videos of the incident went viral on Threads, showing the suspects' vehicle crashing into a road divider at the Jalan Jelatek-Setiawangsa intersection before becoming stuck in the opposite-direction lane.
Footage recorded by members of the public showed one of the suspects fleeing the scene before being apprehended by police with assistance from nearby road users.
Witnesses or those with information on the case can assist the investigation by contacting the Tun H.S. Lee traffic police at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station.

Title: Man found dead in drain near surau in Kepala Batas
Article:
KEPALA BATAS: An unidentified man believed to be in his 40s was found dead in a drain near Surau Permatang Pak Elong today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received a request for assistance from police at 3.52pm.
"When we arrived, we found the body of a man in a drain and carried out recovery operations to move it to a safe area.
"The body was subsequently handed over to the police for further action," he said in a statement.
Seberang Prai Utara police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Abdul Rahman confirmed the discovery.
He said investigations were ongoing, adding that further details would be released later.
The man's identity has yet to be established.

Title: Disaster alert Cell Broadcast System in final phase, live testing on Nov 19
Article:
IPOH: The Cell Broadcast System, a national disaster warning system announced last year, is in its final phase of development, with live testing scheduled for Nov 19.
Developed by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), the system will send disaster alerts directly to mobile phones in affected areas without requiring recipients' phone numbers, SMS services or an internet connection.
It is intended to complement and eventually replace the existing SMS-based disaster warning system, providing faster, more targeted alerts to people in areas at risk.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said timely warnings could give people precious minutes to evacuate and seek shelter before tragedy struck.
"Through this system, warnings can be sent directly to mobile phones in areas at risk without interfering with or accessing personal data," Zahid said.
The system transmits alerts through mobile networks to compatible devices in designated areas. It requires at least one functioning mobile network in the affected area, regardless of the recipient's service provider.
Similar in principle to the United States' Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA), the system delivers emergency messages directly to compatible mobile phones in affected areas. The US also uses the Emergency Alert System to disseminate warnings through radio and television broadcasts.
Zahid said public awareness and trust in accurate information were essential to the system's effectiveness.
"The system is in its final phase, but the public must be aware of it and know how to use it. One important thing we must understand is that technology is only effective if the public trusts accurate information," he said.
The system is also being developed to accommodate people with visual or hearing disabilities and those who have difficulty reading.
According to the Communications Ministry, it is designed to support alerts through vibrations and audio using accessibility functions on compatible mobile devices, including screen readers and voice output.
These features are intended to help users with accessibility needs receive and understand emergency information. Accessibility, device compatibility and the needs of target groups will be considered during testing and implementation.
The ministry said the system had an advantage during disasters that disrupted telecommunications and internet services because alerts were transmitted directly through mobile networks. However, a complete mobile network outage would prevent alerts from being delivered until service was restored.
A network recovery plan, coordinated with disaster management agencies, service providers and other relevant stakeholders, would support the restoration and reactivation of affected network facilities.
Zahid was speaking at the opening of National Preparedness Month 2026, themed "Madani Preparedness, A Shared Responsibility", at the Ipoh Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim.
Zahid said early warnings could give families time to evacuate before floodwaters rose, help senior citizens reach safety and ensure children were moved to safe places.
"That is why early warnings must be delivered on time, be easy to understand and be followed by action. This is why communication is key," he said.
He urged the public to rely on official channels for disaster-related information, warning that unverified reports could undermine response efforts.
He also commended the Fire and Rescue Department, police and Malaysian Armed Forces for their readiness and proactive efforts to assist disaster victims.
Zahid, who is Nadma chairman, said disaster preparedness must be a priority as increasingly unpredictable weather conditions challenged the country's ability to protect lives and property.
Disasters caused RM636.9 million in losses last year, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia, Zahid said.
Of the total, RM380.2 million involved public assets and infrastructure.
Although the figure was lower than the RM933.4 million recorded in 2024, the impact on affected communities remained significant, particularly for those who lost their homes and livelihoods, he said.
He said disaster preparedness must focus not only on saving lives but also on protecting homes, livelihoods and the country's economic assets.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal flood survivor contacted family nine days after disaster, says Masfih
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A Malaysian trekker who returned home safely after Nepal's devastating floods had re-established contact with his family nine days after the disaster, Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (Masfih) said.
Its coordinator and spokesperson, Dr Manivannan Rethinam, said Low contacted his family on Sept 3 after reaching Tipling, where he found electricity and internet access.
Low told his family he was safe and heading towards Kathmandu, Manivannan said.
He clarified the timeline following a five-hour meeting with Low today, saying the 37-day period previously cited referred to the time between the Aug 26 disaster and Low being reported safe, rather than the duration he remained out of contact with his family.
Low was
reported safe on Oct 1
after presenting himself at the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu. He boarded a flight home that day and arrived in Malaysia on Oct 2.
Manivannan, who is also the next of kin of missing Malaysian Komathi Rethinam, said Low told him that he reached Kathmandu on Sept 11 before embarking on a second trek towards Langtang Valley on Sept 13.
Low was stranded in a guest house in the Gosaikunda area for 3 days due to a snowstorm before abandoning the trek and returning to Kathmandu on Sept 29.
Manivannan stressed that Low's safe return must not overshadow the plight of 54 Malaysian nationals who remain unaccounted for.
Based on their last known communications and reported locations, the missing Malaysians were at or near flood-affected areas along the Rasuwagadhi-Kerung border, Timure and Syabrubesi, as well as the downstream Bhote Koshi-Trishuli river corridor.
Nepal's search-and-rescue operations ended on Sept 30.
However, Manivannan urged Malaysian, Nepalese and Chinese authorities to continue recovery and identification efforts, expedite DNA matching and provide families with regular, transparent updates.
He also questioned whether authorities had been promptly informed after Low contacted his family and sought clarification on why DNA samples were subsequently collected, according to his account.
Manivannan further called for clarification on a reported change in Nepalese law concerning the waiting period for declaring missing persons dead in disaster-related cases.
He said Masfih was scheduled to meet Bank Negara Malaysia tomorrow to discuss financial assistance for affected families.
He also renewed requests for meetings with the Attorney-General's Chambers and the prime minister.
"Every family deserves answers. Every missing person deserves to be accounted for," he said, urging authorities to sustain their efforts until the fate of the missing Malaysians was established.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chery Malaysia recalls Omoda 5 vehicles
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Chery Auto Malaysia will recall affected Omoda 5 vehicles, variants C and H, following a recent incident involving the model.
The company said the recall campaign would involve vehicle inspections and replacement of affected components where necessary.
Owners can check whether their vehicles are affected by entering their Vehicle Identification Number on Chery Malaysia's website.
"All inspections and necessary follow-up actions, including component replacement, will be carried out free of charge," it said in a statement today.
It also encouraged Omoda 5 owners seeking added peace of mind to visit an authorised Chery service centre, where its technical teams are ready to assist.
"Chery Auto Malaysia would like to apologise for the inconvenience caused to all our customers. We remain committed to addressing this matter responsibly and ensuring customer safety and confidence," it said, adding that it had been working closely with the Road Transport Department (RTD) since the incident was first reported.
Customers and vehicle owners with enquiries about the campaign can contact the Chery Careline at 03-9388 0888.
Earlier today, it was reported that the RTD had suspended vehicle type approval for the
Chery Omoda 5
following a viral incident in Johor Baru last week, in which the vehicle's rear axle detached completely.
RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the move would also halt new registrations of the model until the technical investigation was completed and potential safety risks identified.

Title: Houthis issue new threat to Saudi airspace after deadly airport attack
Article:
SANAA: Yemen's Houthis issued a new threat to Saudi Arabia's airspace on Sunday after an attack on the kingdom's international airport in Riyadh killed 12 people and wounded hundreds, forcing authorities to stop operations.
Saturday's attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis, who captured swathes of Red Sea coastline in a lightning offensive last month.
While the Iran-backed Houthis stopped short of claiming the strike, they threatened new attacks on the kingdom's airports, except for the holy cities of Makkah and Madinah, warning passengers not to travel.
"The airports and airspace are exposed to targeting and constitute a theatre of operations for our forces," military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X.
The strike came in a week when the group intensified its attacks on the Saudi capital's King Khalid International Airport, where three people were also killed on Thursday, as well as other key targets in the world's top crude oil exporter.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen attributed Saturday's attack to them, calling it a "full-fledged war crime."
A diplomatic source also attributed the strike to a Houthi missile.
The coalition vowed to respond, and on Sunday Houthi media reported two Saudi strikes in Yemen's Houthi-controlled Sanaa governorate.
The assault on Riyadh's airport drew condemnation from the United Nations and world leaders including US President Donald Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.
"We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision," he told reporters.
Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian and one Sudanese were killed, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said.
It said some of the 309 wounded were in serious condition.
A Riyadh-based Western diplomat told AFP the official number of injured did not appear to give a full picture.
The number does not seem to include those with minor wounds, the diplomat said.
OPERATIONS SUSPENDED
Authorities suspended operations at the airport into Sunday, a senior aviation source said, with air traffic monitor Flightradar24 saying the closure was extended until 2100 GMT.
A second aviation source who helps oversee flights to Riyadh confirmed the halt in operations "until further notice."
"Some systems have been damaged – the radar and communications equipment," said the source, adding that runways also needed to be assessed.
One passenger told AFP they witnessed a strike in the airport's domestic terminal.
"I was on gate 403," the witness said. "I saw 401 hit, I saw injured in front of my eyes. Everyone was running."
A French resident of Riyadh said their flight to Europe was cancelled and they would drive to the Qatari capital Doha to fly.
The US, Canadian, German and Spanish embassies in Saudi Arabia warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh airport.
A senior Western diplomat told AFP that several embassies were banning their staff from using the airport "over the next week."
The Saudi-led coalition also announced on Saturday evening the fall of a projectile near Dammam airport in the kingdom's east.
The US embassy in Saudi Arabia on Sunday said staff now require permission to use airports in Dammam and Jeddah, days after a similar order was issued for Riyadh.
DOCTOR CALL-UP
The Riyadh attack prompted health officials to activate a rare mass call-up of doctors, a medical source said.
Schools in Riyadh switched to remote learning for the second time in a month, according to emails seen by AFP that were received by parents.
The European Union's chief called the strike a "dangerous escalation", while Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the "heinous attack" and Gulf neighbours the UAE and Qatar called it a violation of Saudi sovereignty.
Britain, Germany, Iraq and Jordan also denounced it.
It was the deadliest attack in the kingdom since a 2015 suicide bombing. It also came on the eve of Saudi Arabia's high-profile convention and entertainment season.
Riyadh usually hosts a packed calendar of events, including its flagship investment conference drawing foreign leaders and business titans.
Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen's government militarily since 2015.
In Yemen, Saudi-supported government forces were advancing in their counter-offensive against the Houthis around the Bab al-Mandab strait, a key shipping route, military sources said Saturday.
The Houthis claimed to have repelled them.
Claims by both sides have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mother, baby daughter killed in four-vehicle crash in Gua Musang
Article:
GUA MUSANG: A mother and her baby daughter were killed in a four-vehicle accident along the Gua Musang-Kuala Krai road near the Kesedar Paloh 3 settlement here today.
The accident involved three Perodua Myvi cars and a motorcycle, with nine people involved.
Gua Musang Fire and Rescue Station chief Muhammad Azrul Izzham Zulkifli said the department received a report on the incident about 5.10pm.
"When we arrived at the scene, we found that two victims, a mother and her baby daughter, had died, while the driver of a Perodua Myvi was trapped in the wreckage.
"Seven other victims were injured and handed over to the Ministry of Health for further treatment," he said when contacted.

Title: Zahid heads to China tomorrow to boost trade, investment and TVET ties
Article:
BEIJING: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi will undertake a five-day working visit to China from tomorrow to strengthen bilateral ties, particularly in trade, investment, technology and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).
Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad said the visit, from Oct 12 to 16, would include meetings with Chinese government leaders in Beijing before Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, travels to Tianjin to attend the World Vocational and Technical Education Development Conference (WVTEDC) 2026.
He said the Beijing leg would begin with a bilateral meeting with Chinese Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang, followed by a meeting with Public Security Minister Wang Xiaohong and engagements with trade companies to explore economic cooperation opportunities.
"The meeting with Ding is scheduled for Oct 15 at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, with both sides expected to discuss efforts to strengthen existing cooperation and explore new opportunities in investment, technology, human capital and talent development, including TVET.
"Cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) is also expected to feature in the discussions, covering infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy, telecommunications, trade, renewable energy, and science and technology," he told a press conference here today.
Norman said the discussions were also expected to follow up on matters arising from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang during his working visit to China from Sept 22 to 24, further strengthening the Malaysia-China Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
Both sides were also expected to exchange views on their shared commitment to maintaining regional peace and stability through the Asean-China framework, as well as addressing global issues of mutual concern, he said.
In Tianjin, Zahid would attend a dinner hosted by Chinese Education Minister Huai Jinpeng before delivering a keynote address at the opening session of WVTEDC 2026 on Oct 16.
Norman said Zahid, who is also National TVET Council chairman, was expected to be the highest-ranking representative from a foreign government attending the conference, which would bring together 21 ministers and deputy ministers from other countries, with participants from more than 100 countries.
Malaysia's participation would provide opportunities to share best practices, foster cooperation between educational and training institutions, and strengthen industry ties between the two countries, he said.
He said that during his visit to Shanghai last year, Zahid had also sought the Chinese government's cooperation in training Malaysian TVET students, including through institutions such as the Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) and related agencies.
This will be Zahid's third visit to China since assuming the post of deputy prime minister in December 2022. He will be accompanied by senior officials from the Foreign Ministry, Rural and Regional Development Ministry, Higher Education Ministry and the National TVET Council secretariat.
Malaysia-China trade from January to August this year rose 35.1 per cent to RM456.68 billion compared with the same period last year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan Welfare Department provides crisis counselling to stabbed nurse's family
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Kelantan Welfare Department has deployed counsellors to provide crisis intervention to the family of a nurse who was stabbed six times by her husband in Kampung Padang Lepai.
Its director, Che Samsuzuki Che Noh, said the counsellors visited the victim's home last week.
He said the department would also provide other forms of assistance if needed.
"Apart from counselling services, the state Welfare Department will assess the family's needs and provide appropriate assistance," he told reporters after visiting the nurse at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital here today.
Che Samsuzuki was accompanied by Kelantan Women's Development Office director Nik Farhan Muhaimin during the visit.
He said doctors had informed him that the nurse's condition was improving.
"Doctors say her health is improving and they are optimistic that, if there are no complications, the wound dressings could be removed within the next day or two.
"If all goes well, she can be transferred to a normal ward," he said.
Che Samsuzuki said the nurse was also worried about her mother, who lived alone at home.
However, he said the presence of relatives from neighbouring states, including Terengganu, who had come to support the family had helped ease her concerns.
He added that he had also met and spoken to the nurse's eldest daughter, who is studying in Nilai, Negri Sembilan.
"We pray that she and her family will be given the strength to face this difficult challenge," he said.
On Oct 5, the 44-year-old nurse was seriously injured after being stabbed six times by her husband at their home in Kampung Padang Lepai.
Police arrested the 47-year-old suspect, who was remanded for seven days from Oct 6 to assist in the investigation.
Police believe a
dispute over divorce
was the motive for the attack.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah TV3 cameraman hopes Hawana fund will continue helping media workers in need
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: After consulting nine doctors to find the cause of his persistent neck pain, TV3 cameraman Mohammed Fairuz Yazeer is grateful for the assistance he received from Tabung Kasih@Hawana to help ease his medical expenses.
The 35-year-old, who has been with Media Prima Bhd for 17 years, said his neck pain began around the Sabah election in November last year and worsened when he continued working during the Kinabatangan by-election two months later.
"I thought the discomfort was caused by my sleeping position.
"I consulted nine doctors, who suspected that it might be caused by high blood pressure, before I was referred to a neurologist who confirmed that I had a slipped disc," he said.
The father of two said the condition had affected his daily activities, including driving and sleeping.
Fairuz, who is from Putatan, is now undergoing physiotherapy twice a week. He is scheduled for a medical review on Oct 23 to determine whether implant surgery is necessary if his condition does not improve.
He received assistance from Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching during a handover ceremony at the Bernama office here.
"I am grateful for the assistance from the Hawana fund to help cover my treatment expenses. I hope it will continue helping other media colleagues who really need it," he said.
Other recipients were RTM's Floris Philip and Kamarudin Abdullah.
Teo said the fund was established in conjunction with the National Journalists' Day (Hawana) celebrations to assist journalists and veteran media practitioners facing illness, financial hardship and other difficulties.
With support from Telekom Malaysia, the fund has assisted 864 recipients since its establishment in 2023, with total assistance exceeding RM2.5 million.
Also present was Bernama chief executive officer Datin Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Seized vehicles found back in hands of Rohingya detainees, says RTD
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: The Terengganu Road Transport Department has detected cases of seized vehicles returning to the hands of Rohingya detainees after the vehicles had gone through legal proceedings.
Its director, Zamri Samion, said the department had previously detected such cases, in which seized vehicles eventually returned to individuals who had been detained earlier.
He said the cases suggested that some of the foreigners had become integrated into the local community.
"As such, we are conducting continuous operations to address legal violations by foreigners, especially those riding motorcycles without valid driving licences and insurance coverage," he said at a press conference at the department's office here after an Ops Pewa operation today.
Zamri said 305 foreigners were penalised in 22 Ops Pewa operations conducted by the department from January to Oct 11 this year.
During the period, 1,466 summonses were issued and 291 vehicles seized, comprising 247 motorcycles, 36 cars and 8 other vehicles.
"Seized vehicles will not be released until the court case is concluded," he said.
During the 14-day operation from Sept 28 to Oct 11, 69 foreigners were penalised, with 315 summonses issued and 68 vehicles seized.
"Of the vehicles seized during that period, 45 were motorcycles, 17 cars and 6 other vehicles. Apart from that, the RTD also issued two PG.1 notices under Section 59," he said.
Statistics for the same period recorded 350 offences, with driving without a licence accounting for the highest number at 132 cases, followed by 72 cases involving expired motor vehicle licences and 66 cases of having no insurance coverage.
Other technical offences included 16 cases involving registration numbers, 12 involving non-functioning brake lights, two involving side mirrors, one involving tyres and one involving exhausts. Another 31 technical offences and 17 other offences were also recorded.
Zamri said Ops Pewa was conducted following public complaints about foreigners using vehicles without valid documents, particularly in the Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus districts.
The operation also involved undercover tactics to detect offenders and deployed 40 personnel from the Terengganu RTD, its Kemaman and Besut branches, and the Kijal, Bukit Besi and Air Sejuk enforcement stations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'I just want justice for my mother': Daughter of stabbed nurse
Article:
KOTA BARU: The family of a nurse who was stabbed six times allegedly by her husband does not seek retribution against the suspect but hopes justice will be served.
Her eldest daughter, Nik Ruziany Nik Ahmad Ruzi, 19, said she hoped what happened to her mother would never happen to anyone else.
"I do not wish for him (the suspect) to receive severe punishment as retribution.
"I only hope that my mother gets justice so that this does not happen to anyone else," she told reporters.
Ruziany, the eldest of two siblings, was speaking after receiving a visit from Kelantan Social Welfare Department director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital here today, where her mother is receiving treatment.
She also shared an encouraging update on her mother's recovery, saying the victim had slowly started speaking again.
"My mother has slowly started speaking again, but what concerns her most is the well-being of her elderly mother and the safety of her children," she said.
The 44-year-old nurse was allegedly stabbed six times in the body and neck by her 47-year-old husband in Ketereh on Oct 5.
Police have arrested the suspect to assist in the investigation.
The case is being investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt with a dangerous weapon. The offence carries a jail term of up to 20 years and a fine or whipping upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Damai Perdana residents move out over safety fears after landslide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Several families at Pangsapuri Damai Perdana in Cheras have decided to move out over safety concerns following a landslide near their apartment last month.
A check today found residents taking advantage of the weekend to remove their belongings as they prepared to leave their homes.
Private sector worker Selamat Mat Zain, 48, said he decided to move because he was worried about his family's safety and felt the authorities had yet to provide adequate assurance that it was safe to remain there.
"I decided to move because I am worried about my family's safety. Although we have been allowed to return, there is no assurance of safety here.
"No repair works have been carried out by any party following the landslide near our home," he said when met at the apartment today.
[[nid:1553231]]
He said residents were also facing other problems, including a lack of water supply.
"I will be moving to a new home starting tomorrow to ensure my family's safety, as I am worried the same incident will recur," he said.
It was reported earlier that residents living near the slope at Pangsapuri Damai Perdana had been told to move following the landslide near the building on Sept 22.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar was reported to have said the department received an emergency call at 9.03pm about the incident near Block D of the apartment.
The landslide is believed to have been caused by a leaking underground water pipe, and the affected slope is estimated to be about four metres high.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'No corruption scandals': Loke hails Aminuddin's clean record
Article:
SEREMBAN: Pakatan Harapan (PH) Negri Sembilan has recorded what DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke described as an achievement to be proud of, with no corruption scandals or integrity issues during the coalition's eight years in power under former Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun.
Loke said DAP would continue to support Aminuddin, who is also Negri Sembilan PKR chairman, to lead PH in the state.
He said the coalition had recorded various achievements under Aminuddin's leadership, including improvements in reserves, development, infrastructure and investment.
"One of the most important things we should be proud of is that during our eight years in the state government, with him (Aminuddin) serving as menteri besar, there were no corruption scandals that plagued the administration.
"The administration's record remains clean. There is nothing that can be levelled against Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun or our fellow executive councillors," he said in his speech at the 24th DAP Negri Sembilan Annual Convention here today.
Also present were Aminuddin and state DAP chairman J. Arul Kumar.
Loke, who is also transport minister, said Aminuddin had carried out his responsibilities as menteri besar to the best of his ability, in line with the party's aim of bringing about change and reform.
The Seremban member of parliament also expressed appreciation for Aminuddin's contributions to the development of Negri Sembilan.
"We have stood together through good times and bad. We have carried the burden together. DAP wants to express its unwavering support for him to continue leading PH Negri Sembilan because his integrity has been tested and proven. This is very important to DAP," he said.
Aminuddin was appointed PH Negri Sembilan chairman in 2017 and was the coalition's first menteri besar in the state.
In the Negri Sembilan election in August, Aminuddin, who contested the Linggi state seat for the first time, lost in a three-cornered fight.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umrah pilgrims' families anxious after flights diverted amid Riyadh airport attack
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Families of Malaysians travelling to Saudi Arabia for umrah have expressed concern after some flights were reportedly diverted to Madinah following an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.
Posts on social media platform Threads showed family members seeking reassurance after their relatives encountered flight diversions amid security concerns.
One user, Bobsazali, said his brother-in-law had informed him that their flight was diverted to Madinah after departing from Kuala Lumpur International Airport.
The aircraft subsequently continued its journey to Jeddah, where the passengers landed safely. Bobsazali later shared an update from his brother-in-law confirming their safe arrival.
Another user, f.azzahra88, said her flight had also landed safely in Jeddah after being diverted to Madinah.
In her initial post, she said the aircraft had circled while attempting to land in Jeddah before being redirected to Madinah, where it landed safely. Passengers were then asked to remain inside the aircraft while awaiting further instructions.
In a subsequent post, she said the flight had received clearance to resume its journey to Jeddah.
Meanwhile, Aishah Izzati Abdul Rahman, 31, who is scheduled to perform umrah, said she was due to fly to Jeddah on Oct 16 and had yet to receive any updates from her travel agent about possible disruptions.
"We have been told to gather at KLIA at 8pm on Oct 15," she said.
Fauzana Ismail, 43, who had performed umrah, said she and her group were at King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah awaiting their return flight to Malaysia when the incident occurred.
Although they were not directly affected, she said they remained concerned about the situation as they were still in Saudi Arabia.
"Although we were not directly affected, we were still worried because we were in Saudi Arabia. Naturally, we felt concerned about the situation, especially as we were waiting to board our flight home.
"We couldn't stop praying that everything would go smoothly and that we would arrive home safely. Although we were worried, we tried to remain calm and hoped for the best.
"Alhamdulillah, we arrived home safely," she said when contacted.
Despite the concerns, the Umrah and Haj Travel Agencies Association (Papuh) said it had received no reports of flight cancellations among its members following the attack.
Its president, Datuk Seri Razali Mohd Sham, said pilgrims who had booked flights through travel agents and were scheduled to depart in the coming days had not reported any problems so far.
"Based on the information available to me, I have not heard of any reports in our group indicating that flights have been cancelled.
"For those who have already made their bookings and are scheduled to depart, there have been no issues reported so far," he said.
Razali added that most flights from Malaysia to Saudi Arabia arrived at either King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah or Prince Mohammad bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Madinah.
International media reported that 12 people were killed and 309 injured in the attack at King Khalid International Airport.
The incident occurred amid reports of an increase in Houthi missile attacks against Saudi Arabia in recent weeks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Retiree loses RM118,000 in fake share investment scam
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A 66-year-old retiree lost RM118,000 in savings after signing up on a fake share investment website that led to unauthorised withdrawals from his bank and Touch 'n Go accounts.
Johor Baru (South) police chief, Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei, said the victim discovered the losses on Sept 15, after 16 transactions totalling RM118,000 were made without his knowledge between July 28 and Aug 4.
The victim became interested in investing in shares in early July after coming across the website.
He registered on the platform and provided his personal details, including information linked to his bank and Touch 'n Go accounts.
Investigations found that nine transactions were made from his bank account, to the tune of RM77,702, while another seven withdrawals drained RM40,298 from his Touch 'n Go account.
"The total loss of RM118,000 involved the victim's personal savings," Azrul Hisham said in a statement.
Police are checking the bank accounts involved, obtaining transaction records from the financial institutions and working to identify and arrest those responsible.
The case is being probed under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating and Section 4(1) of the Computer Crimes Act 1997.
If convicted under Section 420, an offender faces imprisonment of up to 10 years, whipping and a fine.
The applicable penalties under the Computer Crimes Act depend on the specific offence established.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Schools in Pahang to operate as usual tomorrow
Article:
KUANTAN: All schools in Pahang will operate as usual tomorrow, says the Pahang Education Department.
In a statement, the department said any changes would be announced from time to time through the respective district education offices based on the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
"During the haze, all teachers, pupils, Members of Implementing Groups (AKP) and the school community are encouraged to wear face masks for everyone's safety and health. Ensure face masks properly cover the nose and mouth.
"Parents, guardians and the school community are advised to always follow official announcements from the schools.
"The safety, health and welfare of pupils and the education community remain the priority of the Pahang Education Department," the statement said.
Last Friday, all educational institutions in the
Rompin district
under the supervision of the Pahang Education Department were temporarily closed until conditions return to safe levels and further instructions are issued.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: All schools in Johor, four Selangor districts closed tomorrow, says Fadhlina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All schools in Johor and schools under four district education offices in Selangor will be closed tomorrow as the haze situation in the country remains hazardous.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said the four district education offices covered the areas of Bangsar Pudu, Hulu Langat, Gombak and Petaling Perdana.
However, she said that schools in Melaka, Penang, Putrajaya, Labuan, Perak, Pahang, Negri Sembilan, Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah, Perlis, Sabah and Sarawak would remain open.
"For Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, schools under PPDs (district education offices) other than those stated will also operate as usual," she said.
She said state education directors have been told to set up a Haze Monitoring Task Force involving the state education departments and district education offices.
Fadhlina said parents, guardians and teachers were asked to keep updated with the latest information on school operations through the official platforms of the Ministry and related departments.
"Parents and school communities are asked to refer to official notices from the Education Ministry, the state education departments and their respective PPDs for any latest developments," she said.
Earlier, the ministry said in a statement that the
operating status
of schools would be determined based on daily monitoring of Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Johor postpones special school admission test; schools remain shut until Oct 16
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Special School Admission Assessment (PKSK), scheduled for tomorrow, has been postponed due to the haze, with a new date to be announced by the Johor Education Department.
The
assessment
is used for admission to selected special schools, and the postponement follows the state's extension of school closures until Oct 16 to protect pupils' health and safety.
Johor Education and Information Committee chairman, Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali, said the five-day closure extension was necessary amid deteriorating air quality.
"Our priority remains ensuring the safety and well-being of Johor's children," he said, thanking the public for their concern and feedback.
He said the Year Four Learning Matrix (MPT4) and other affected assessments would also be rescheduled.
Home-based teaching and learning (PdPR) will continue throughout the closure.
Teachers and school staff are allowed to work from home, while officers at the state and district education departments will report for duty as usual.
The department will continue monitoring air pollution index readings and take further action based on developments and directives from the education ministry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: HRD Corp to support 3 million training opportunities under 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) will continue to utilise RM3 billion from its levy funds to support three million training opportunities, in line with the government's efforts to strengthen skills development and workforce competitiveness.
The initiative will focus on professional certifications, upskilling aligned with industry needs, and improving the quality of and access to training.
HRD Corp said the measures supported the 13th Malaysia Plan's (13MP) target of having skilled workers make up 35 per cent of the workforce by 2030.
Its chief executive, Datuk Shamir Aziz, said the emphasis on human capital development in the 2027 Budget reflected the importance of strengthening workers' skills to navigate economic changes and evolving industry needs.
He said HRD Corp would continue to focus on industry-relevant training, recognise professional certifications and the strategic utilisation of levy funds to ensure employers' investments in skills development delivered meaningful value to workers and businesses.
"Efforts to upskill and provide reskilling opportunities must continue to be expanded across all segments of society to create more employment and career advancement opportunities, while supporting the development of a more skilled, productive and competitive workforce," he said.
Under the 2027 Budget, RM40 million has been allocated to HRD Corp for the Madani Professional Caregiver Skills initiative, which aims to strengthen the country's care economy by developing a skilled and professional caregiving workforce.
The initiative is expected to benefit up to 8,000 participants, particularly school leavers, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) graduates, homemakers, jobseekers and unemployed individuals interested in pursuing careers in the care sector.
Funding will cover training costs, attendance allowances and training kits.
Training will cover elderly care, infant and childcare, care for persons with disabilities, postnatal care and community care.
HRD Corp said the initiative aimed to develop a skilled caregiving workforce while creating career pathways in the growing sector.
The agency, under the purview of the Human Resources Ministry, said it would continue working with industries, employers and training providers to ensure skills development met industry needs, benefited the people and supported economic growth.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Schools in Melaka, Negri, Pahang, Putrajaya to reopen tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Pahang and Putrajaya, as well as several areas in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, will resume normal operations tomorrow.
In  KUALA LUMPUR, the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Education Department said MOE educational institutions under the Sentul and Keramat District Education Offices (PPDs) would reopen tomorrow, following a decline in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the areas for three consecutive days.
"The latest reading was at a moderate level, with an API of 84 recorded at the CA15W Batu Muda station as of 2 pm today. As such, the implementation of Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) and the Work From Home (WFH) directive for these areas has been terminated," Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Education Department said in a statement.
However, the department said schools under the Bangsar/Pudu PPD would remain closed until further notice, as air quality remained at an unhealthy level, with an API reading of 152 recorded at the CA16W Cheras station during the same period.
It said that to ensure continuity of teaching and learning, PdPR and the WFH directive for teachers and Implementing Group Staff (AKP) under the Bangsar/Pudu PPD would continue.
In SELANGOR, the Selangor Education Department said all schools under the administration of the Hulu Langat, Gombak and Petaling Perdana PPDs would remain closed based on the latest API readings.
In a statement, the department also said all schools in other districts in the state would operate as usual tomorrow.
"Teachers and parents are advised to follow official updates from the authorities on developments in air quality and relevant school operation directives.
"Further information on school operations and reopening will be announced through the official channels of the MOE and the department," the statement said.
In MELAKA, schools will resume normal operations tomorrow, as air quality readings remained at moderate levels below 100, according to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) as of 2pm, with Alor Gajah recording 91, Bukit Rambai 94 and Bandaraya Melaka 96.
In NEGERI SEMBILAN, the Negri Sembilan Education Department also said all MOE educational institutions would operate as usual tomorrow based on the latest air quality monitoring.
It also advised students experiencing respiratory symptoms or those in high-risk groups to wear face masks as a precautionary measure.
In PAHANG, the Pahang Education Department also said all schools in the state would operate as usual tomorrow, with the haze situation and API readings being continuously monitored from time to time through the respective PPDs.
In  PUTRAJAYA, the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department said all schools under its administration would operate as usual tomorrow, following API readings remaining below the 150 threshold.
According to the department, analysis of API readings showed a consistent decline over the past three days, with the API standing at 70 as of 2 pm today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fama to add 241 agri-food outlets under 13MP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama) will expand its agri-food marketing network with 241 new outlets under the 13th Malaysia Plan.
This will be supported by a RM40 million allocation for outlet rejuvenation.
Fama said the initiative aims to strengthen market access for agricultural producers and entrepreneurs while making the distribution and sale of local agri-food products more efficient and attractive to consumers.
Fama senior director of market institutions division Intan Suraya Ibeni Hajar said the rejuvenation programme goes beyond upgrading the physical appearance of its outlets, emphasising building a modern business ecosystem.
"Rejuvenation is not just about making outlets look better.
"More importantly, it is about developing a more modern business ecosystem so that outlets remain relevant, entrepreneurs become more competitive and consumers have better access to agri-food products," she said.
The 241 new outlets will comprise various marketing channels. They include Pasar Tani, Agrobazaar Rakyat, Agrobazaar Kedai Rakyat, Gerai Buah-Buahan Segar and Karavan Tani.
At the same time, Fama plans to upgrade 411 existing outlets to provide a more conducive, organised and consumer-friendly environment.
The agency is also looking to modernise how entrepreneurs conduct business, with greater adoption of cashless transactions, social media and digital platforms to help them reach customers beyond physical outlets.
This is expected to give small and micro entrepreneurs additional channels to promote their products and expand their customer base as consumer purchasing habits increasingly shift towards digital platforms.
The rejuvenation programme also covers the wholesale segment.
Fama is targeting the development of 15 Agrobazaar Rakyat Pemborongan outlets and four outlets within the wholesale ecosystem.
The expansion is intended to strengthen connections between producers, wholesalers, retailers and consumers, creating a more structured marketing chain for agricultural products.
Fama will also conduct 480 promotional and advocacy programmes to increase awareness of its outlets and encourage consumers to purchase locally produced agri-food products.
Beyond physical infrastructure, entrepreneur development will remain a key component.
A total of 32 training and capacity-building programmes have been planned, comprising two entrepreneur conventions, 20 courses and 10 Pasar Tani Student programmes.
"We want young people to see the agri-food sector as an area with entrepreneurial potential.
"With technology, digital marketing and more modern business models, there is considerable room for the younger generation to explore the sector," said Intan Suraya.
Meanwhile, the Agro-Jaja project will benefit 100 hawkers at RTC Kelantan through business image development and equipment support.
The initiative underscores Fama's broader role in food security, where strengthening production must be matched by reliable and accessible marketing channels.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tax breaks, wage hike headline 2027 Budget surprises: CIMB Securities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget has delivered larger-than-expected tax relief and a higher minimum wage, offering support for household spending while raising cost pressures for businesses, said CIMB Securities.
The basic individual tax relief rises from RM9,000 to RM12,000, while tax rates for chargeable income between RM70,001 and RM150,000 will be cut by one percentage point.
CIMB Securities analyst Ivy Ng Lee Fang said the measures could generate annual tax savings of up to RM1,600 for about five million taxpayers, supporting middle-income consumption.
Businesses will also benefit from lower corporate tax rates for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and expanded sales tax recovery for qualifying machinery and production inputs.
The minimum wage will rise 17.6 per cent to RM2,000 a month from June 2027, benefiting more than four million workers. However, MSMEs with annual sales below RM50 million are exempted.
The government's 2027 fiscal deficit target of 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product is also slightly better than the 3.4 per cent forecast, despite the 2026 deficit estimate being revised to 3.6 per cent.
Ng said the budget is "neutral to mildly positive" for Malaysian equities, with higher disposable income and targeted assistance expected to support consumer companies such as 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd, Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd, MR D.I.Y. Group (M) Bhd and QL Resources Bhd.
The RM83 billion development expenditure allocation and continued infrastructure investment favour construction players Gamuda Bhd and Malayan Cement Bhd.
Housing incentives and improved connectivity in Johor could benefit UEM Sunrise Bhd and Eco World Development Group Bhd.
Renewable energy and technology companies could gain from extended green investment incentives and semiconductor funding, she said.
Healthcare providers KPJ Healthcare Bhd and IHH Healthcare Bhd may also benefit from opportunities linked to public hospital outsourcing and MediAsas.
Ng said higher minimum wages will increase costs for labour-intensive plantation, glove manufacturing, retail and services businesses, although implementation from June 2027 limits the immediate earnings impact.
Companies that improve productivity through efficiency measures and automation will be better placed to offset higher labour costs.
She said overall, the minimum-wage increase is expected to have a limited direct impact on aggregate FBM KLCI earnings in 2027, while the budget's consumption and investment measures provide selective support for listed companies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TH depositors' money not used to fund Perkeso for religious workers - Zulkifli
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan said that Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) depositors' savings were not used to pay Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributions for 40,000 mosque personnel and takmir teachers nationwide.
He said a special government allocation fully funded the contributions, channeled through TH as the implementing agency.
Zulkifli said the government's decision to fully fund the contributions recognises religious personnel's service and helps safeguard their welfare, social protection and wellbeing.
"Any claims or assumptions that pilgrims' savings have been used are entirely untrue and speculative," he said in a statement today.
The beneficiaries include imams, bilals, mosque caretakers and takmir teachers serving Muslim communities nationwide.
Zulkifli said the government is committed to ensuring that TH upholds integrity in managing its trust funds and maintains transparent corporate governance in accordance with Syariah principles.
He said the government will continue to prioritise the welfare of mosque personnel and takmir teachers to safeguard religious institutions and support the development of the Muslim community in Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri Sembilan schools to reopen tomorrow as air quality improves
Article:
SEREMBAN: All Education Ministry (MOE) educational institutions in Negri Sembilan will resume normal operations tomorrow following a temporary closure last Friday due to poor air quality.
In a statement today, the Negri Sembilan Education Department said the decision was made after monitoring prevailing weather conditions and the latest Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
"The department wishes to inform that all MOE educational institutions in Negri Sembilan will operate as usual on Monday, Oct 12 based on the monitoring of current conditions and the latest API readings," the statement read.
However, school administrators have been instructed to continue monitoring air quality, comply with existing guidelines and take the necessary precautions to safeguard the health and safety of pupils and school personnel.
The department also advised pupils to wear face masks as a precaution, particularly those experiencing respiratory symptoms or belonging to high-risk groups.
"The Negri Sembilan Education Department will continue to monitor developments closely and issue official updates should there be any changes. Parents and guardians are advised to rely on official department channels for the latest information," it added.
All schools in Negri Sembilan were ordered to close last Friday after API monitoring stations in Nilai, Seremban and Port Dickson recorded unhealthy air quality levels for three consecutive days.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FIA sees bigger motorsport role for Malaysia beyond F1
Article:
THE successful return to the Formula 1 (F1) spotlight at Sepang has put Malaysia's motorsport credentials back on the global stage and FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem believes the chequered flag should be only the beginning.
Rather than chasing an F1 comeback alone, Malaysia has the ingredients to become a broader motorsport hub, drawing on its established racing culture, passionate fan base and growing pool of enthusiasts, he said.
"Malaysia, to me, is not only about Formula 1. Malaysia, to me, is about motorsport," Ben Sulayem told the New Straits Times and three other media a few hours before the rain-delayed Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia last Sunday.
[[nid:1553175]]
He said the country could look beyond F1 to a wider FIA racing portfolio, including the World Rally Championship, Formula E, World Endurance Championship and cross-country events, while strengthening the grassroots pipeline through karting and rallying.
"You give them karting. You give them cheaper karting. You give them cheaper cross-car. You give them cheaper rally cars. This is the way to go," he said.
Ben Sulayem said the FIA's role is not simply to add more F1 races, but to broaden participation in motorsport and create pathways for enthusiasts and young competitors.
He said Malaysia had already demonstrated that it has a strong motorsport following, with the response to the return of international racing at Sepang showing that interest had remained despite the nine-year absence of F1.
The 65-year-old Emirati was particularly impressed by Malaysian fans and officials during the F1 race weekend, describing them as knowledgeable and passionate.
"The educated fans and the educated staff. You have a very amazing culture," he said.
[[nid:1553174]]
He also praised the cooperation between Malaysian and Bahraini officials, saying the two sides worked together effectively on the ground.
"What really amazed me is the harmonisation between Malaysian and Bahrain. Not at the top level. I'm talking about here on the ground. This is very, very impressive," he said.
For Ben Sulayem, that response demonstrated that Malaysia's motorsport passion had not disappeared during its absence from F1.
"They were there, but they were waiting for an opportunity to show their passion," he said.
He also highlighted the potential for Malaysia and the wider Asia Pacific region to contribute more to the global motorsport ecosystem, pointing to the region's economic strength, manufacturing base and diverse automotive culture.
While F1 remains the sport's biggest global platform, Ben Sulayem said the FIA's broader objective was to grow motorsport across multiple disciplines.
"We have to continue the WRC… There is the World Endurance Championship, Formula E, all of this. And now the cross-country. There is so much," he said.
For Malaysia, that could mean using the renewed attention on Sepang as a springboard for a wider motorsport strategy rather than treating F1 as the sole measure of success.
Ben Sulayem said Malaysia had the ingredients needed to build that future.
"You have a great fan base. You have enthusiasts. You have people who love motorsport. What do you give them?" he asked.
In the end, Sepang's unexpected return could hardly have produced a more compelling advertisement for the circuit, in sporting terms.
The race was delayed by heavy rain, the opening laps were shaped by treacherous conditions and tyre choices, and multiple Safety Car periods repeatedly changed the complexion of the contest.
Max Verstappen eventually emerged as the winner, but the result was far from straightforward.
He lost the lead at the start before recovering it through a combination of pace and strategy, while Kimi Antonelli held second and Lewis Hamilton produced one of the drives of the race to climb from deep in the field to third.
Charles Leclerc also recovered strongly to fourth.
[[nid:1553173]]
That unpredictability played directly into Sepang's strengths. The circuit has long been known for its demanding layout, high tyre degradation and tropical weather, and the 2026 race once again showed how those ingredients can produce genuine strategic and sporting drama.
Just as importantly, Malaysia demonstrated that its nine-year absence had not diminished its ability to stage F1 at the highest level.
The successful organisation of a race brought in at short notice - replacing the cancelled Bahrain event - gave Sepang an opportunity to prove its operational readiness as well as its sporting credentials.
The chequered flag, therefore, may not mark Malaysia's F1 story.
If the country can build on the momentum generated by a memorable race and translate it into a wider motorsport proposition, Sepang's return could prove to be less a one-off encore and more the reopening of a door to the global racing world.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: M'sia condemns deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia, urges peaceful resolution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has strongly condemned the deadly attacks targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia on Saturday (Oct 10), which claimed lives, left several people injured and disrupted airport operations and commercial flights.
In a statement on Sunday, the Foreign Ministry reaffirmed Malaysia's solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its support for the Kingdom's efforts to safeguard its sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security.
"Malaysia is seriously concerned by the recent escalation of hostilities and violence, and urges all parties to respect international law and pursue a peaceful resolution through dialogue and diplomacy, towards restoring lasting peace, security and stability in the region," the statement read.
The ministry said Malaysia also extended its heartfelt condolences and sympathies over the loss of lives and wished those injured a speedy recovery.
In a statement on Sunday, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said 12 people were killed and 309 injured in Saturday's attack on the King Khalid International Airport.
Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, and one each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine, and Sudan were killed in the attack.
Earlier, Malaysia's Foreign Ministry reported that there were no Malaysian casualties following Saturday's attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and a projectile landing near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Temporary lane closures, diversions on Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway starting Oct 12 for elevated U-turn works
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 11 — The rightmost lanes along both directions of the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway will be temporarily closed from October 12 to February 28, 2027, to facilitate the next phase of construction works for an elevated U-turn.
IJM Land Berhad in a statement today said the closure would affect the median-side rightmost lanes of the George Town-bound and Bayan Lepas-bound carriageways.
The master developer of THE LIGHT Waterfront Penang said the lane closures and traffic diversions were necessary to provide a safe working area for the construction works.
“The initial phase of construction for the elevated U-turn was successfully completed in early September, and upon completion, the elevated U-turn is expected to complement the Air Itam Bypass, helping to improve road connectivity and traffic flow along the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway.
“Motorists are advised to plan their journeys ahead, follow directional signage, and exercise caution when approaching the affected areas,” according to the statement.
IJM Land said further updates would be provided as construction progressed, adding that it appreciated the public’s patience and understanding throughout the construction period. — Bernama

Title: Sungai Golok river basin project: Scope, design adjustments aim to provide long-term flood protection
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 11 — Adjustments to the scope and design of the Sungai Golok Integrated River Basin (PLSB) project in Kelantan are among the factors affecting its implementation timeline and cost.
The Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA) said the adjustments were made to meet current needs, taking into account climate change, infrastructure requirements, actual site conditions and the needs of local residents.
“Among the adjustments made were those involving land acquisition, changes to the project alignment and drainage system capacity to ensure that the project’s design and scope were suited to current conditions and that the flood mitigation system could function more effectively.
“These adjustments are crucial to ensuring that the infrastructure provides reliable, sustainable and safe long-term flood protection for residents in flood-prone areas,” the statement said today.
Earlier, Deputy Minister of Energy Transition and Water Transformation Datuk Seri Abdul Rahman Mohamad, accompanied by senior officials from PETRA and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID), visited the project site to assess progress and ensure that work was carried out efficiently, systematically and according to schedule.
A Bernama survey of the flood mitigation works under the Sungai Golok Integrated River Basin Development project in Pasir Mas October 11, 2026. — Bernama pic
The statement said PETRA would continue to ensure that the project was implemented in accordance with the principles of prudent and responsible governance, with the safety and well-being of the people remaining a priority.
“Close cooperation between the Federal Government, through PETRA and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID), and the state government will continue to be strengthened to ensure that project-related issues are addressed effectively and in a coordinated manner.
“PETRA also welcomes constructive recommendations and feedback from stakeholders to improve the efficiency of project implementation, while ensuring that environmental sustainability and the well-being of the people remain key priorities,” the statement said.
The ministry also reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that public funds were managed prudently, transparently and accountably, with emphasis on the quality of project implementation and benefits to the public.
It said these efforts would be further strengthened to ensure the more effective implementation of water infrastructure and coastal restoration projects, particularly in mitigating the risks of flooding and coastal erosion.
On the project’s implementation status, PETRA said Phase 1 had achieved 73.01 per cent physical progress, while Phases 2 and 3 had recorded 3.16 per cent and 24.18 per cent, respectively.
“Phase 1 is expected to be completed in July 2027, while Phases 2 and 3 are scheduled for completion in October 2028 and April 2029, respectively,” the statement added. — Bernama

Title: DPM Zahid to lead Malaysian delegation on five-day China working visit
Article:
BEIJING, Oct 11 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi will undertake a five-day working visit to China beginning tomorrow to strengthen bilateral ties, particularly in trade, investment, technology, and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).
Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad said the visit, from October 12 to 16, would include a series of meetings with Chinese government leaders in Beijing before Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, travels to Tianjin to attend the World Vocational and Technical Education Development Conference (WVTEDC) 2026.
He said the agenda in Beijing would begin with a bilateral meeting with Chinese Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang, followed by a meeting with Public Security Minister Wang Xiaohong and several engagements with trade companies to explore opportunities for economic cooperation.
“The meeting with Ding is scheduled for October 15 at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, with both sides expected to discuss efforts to strengthen existing cooperation and explore new opportunities in investment, technology, and human capital and talent development, including TVET.
“Cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) is also expected to feature in the discussions, covering infrastructure, artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy, telecommunications, trade, renewable energy, and science and technology,” he told a press conference here today.
Norman said the discussions were also expected to follow up on several matters arising from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s meeting with Premier Li Qiang during his working visit to China from Sept 22 to 24, further strengthening the Malaysia-China Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
He said both sides were also expected to exchange views on their shared commitment to maintaining regional peace and stability through the Asean-China framework, as well as addressing global issues of mutual concern.
Norman said that in Tianjin, the Deputy Prime Minister would attend a dinner hosted by Chinese Education Minister Huai Jinpeng before delivering a keynote address at the opening session of WVTEDC 2026 on October 16.
He said Ahmad Zahid, who is also the National TVET Council chairman, was expected to be the highest-ranking representative from a foreign government attending the conference, which would bring together 21 ministers and deputy ministers from other countries, with participation from more than 100 countries.
Norman said Malaysia’s participation would provide opportunities to share best practices, foster cooperation between educational and training institutions, and strengthen industry ties between the two countries.
He said that during his visit to Shanghai last year, Ahmad Zahid had also sought the Chinese government’s cooperation in training Malaysian TVET students, including through institutions such as the Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) and related agencies.
This will be Ahmad Zahid’s third visit to China since assuming the post of Deputy Prime Minister in December 2022. He will be accompanied by senior officials from the Foreign Ministry, Rural and Regional Development Ministry, Higher Education Ministry and the National TVET Council secretariat.
Malaysia-China trade for the January-August 2026 period rose 35.1 per cent to RM456.68 billion compared with the same period last year. — Bernama

Title: MCMC boosts UMS internet coverage with 1,010 new Wi-Fi access points, says Teo Nie Ching
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has added approximately 1,010 Wi-Fi access points at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) to expand internet coverage on the campus.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said that this initiative is part of MCMC’s ongoing efforts to ensure that the people of Sabah, particularly students and higher education institution (IPT) communities, have access to high-quality internet services.
She added that the initiative is implemented through a project involving the addition of Wi-Fi access points in public universities nationwide, with MCMC utilising its own funds to support the implementation.
“In Malaysia, we have 20 public universities, and MCMC is once again using its own funds to add Wi-Fi access points in universities, and UMS is certainly among the universities involved in this project,” she said during a live interview session with SABAHfm at the Ministry of Communications Integrated Complex here today.
Also present were Bernama Chief Executive Officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin and Sabah Broadcasting Department Director Mohd Yusni Mohamed Ali.
Teo said the addition will make internet coverage on the campus more comprehensive, thereby enhancing internet access convenience for the university community.
In the meantime, Teo expressed hope that the implementation of the second phase of the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA) will further improve 4G coverage in rural and sparsely populated areas in Sabah.
She stated that although these areas lack commercial value for telecommunications companies, the ministry will utilise the latest technologies, such as satellites, to resolve connectivity issues.
In conjunction with her visit to the complex, Teo also inspected the development and operations of departments and facilities under the Ministry of Communications, including the SABAHfm Contrabass Studio, the Entertainment and Music Studio, and the television set for the programme “Kami Bah Ini”. — Bernama

Title: ‘Lighad’ issue: Quran must not be subject to mockery, says religious affairs minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The sanctity of the Quran must always be upheld as it serves as the ultimate source of divine guidance for Muslims, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said.
He said mocking or insulting the Quran was an irresponsible act that could hurt the religious sensitivities of Muslims.
Responding to the viral issue concerning the word “lighad”, which appears in Verse 18 of Surah al-Hasyr, Zulkifli said the word meant “tomorrow” and had a contextual meaning pertaining to preparations for the Hereafter.
“The term carries a specific meaning in the Quran and should not be distorted or made a subject of mockery by associating it with other words in a manner that demeans the religion.
“Therefore, all parties must understand the true meaning and context of Quranic verses and refrain from mocking the sacred text,” he said in a statement today.
Zulkifli said mutual respect and responsible communication were essential to preserving religious sanctity and maintaining harmony in a multireligious society.
He said any conduct deemed disrespectful towards Islam should be brought to the attention of the relevant authorities for investigation and appropriate action under the law.
A social media influencer questioned Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s use of the word “lighad” when tabling the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat and sarcastically associated it with another word.
