Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said yesterday that the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) were seeking to locate the individual to record a statement to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Zelensky says Ukraine ready to halt refinery strikes if Russia stops hitting energy grid
Article:
KYIV, Oct 11 — Ukraine would be ready to stop hitting Russian oil refineries if Russia curbed its attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Sunday, after criticism from US counterpart Donald Trump.
Tensions between the two leaders have flared since Friday, when Trump announced a deal that would see Russia release large amounts of diesel onto global energy markets in exchange for sanctions relief.
Zelensky described the deal as a “weak decision”, saying it would encourage Russia to keep attacking Ukraine, but Trump said Saturday that Ukraine’s strikes were to blame for rising fuel prices.
Prices at US gasoline and diesel pumps have surged since late February, when joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran prompted Tehran to block the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway used for oil exports from the Gulf.
“Ukraine will be ready to stop striking Russian oil refineries if Russia stops striking our energy infrastructure. Any de-escalation steps must be reciprocal and backed by real guarantees,” Zelensky said on X.
Russia has launched waves of attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure since invading in February 2022, knocking out power and heating to millions during winter months.
Ukraine’s largest private energy provider, DTEK, announced fresh power outages in the capital Kyiv on Sunday.
The row between Zelensky and Trump comes weeks before closely-fought US elections dominated by voter frustration over the cost of living. — AFP

Title: Two dead, including baby girl, in Gua Musang crash involving three cars and motorcycle
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Oct 11 — Two people, including a baby girl, were killed in an accident involving three cars and a motorcycle on the Gua Musang-Kuala Krai Road, Kampung Paloh 3, here this afternoon.
The Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) stated in a release that the 5.10pm accident also resulted in seven other individuals being injured, including two who were reported to be in critical condition.
According to the statement, the accident involved three Perodua Myvi cars and a Modenas motorcycle.
“One Perodua Myvi driver was reported to be critically injured and trapped, but was successfully rescued by members of the public before the arrival of the fire and rescue team,” the statement read.
All victims were subsequently handed over to the Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) medical team for further action, it added.
Following the incident, a team from the Gua Musang Fire and Rescue Station (BBP), which arrived at the scene at 6.08pm, carried out cleanup operations for accident debris and oil spills. — Bernama

Title: Wanita PKR lodges police report against Eric See-To over alleged mockery of Quranic verse
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 11 — Wanita PKR has lodged a police report against the owner of the Facebook account Eric See-To, also known as Lim Sian See, over a post allegedly mocking an expression related to a Quranic verse.
Wanita PKR executive committee member Farahida Fauzi said the report was lodged at the Kuantan District Police Headquarters at about noon today to enable the matter to be investigated.
“I urge the authorities to conduct an immediate, transparent and impartial investigation. If a violation of the law is established, firm action must be taken without delay,” she said in a statement today.
Farahida, who is also Wanita PKR Pahang deputy chief, reminded the public not to make fun of religion to attract attention, provoke others or seek popularity.
Yesterday, Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh urged the individual to issue a public apology for allegedly mocking the use of the word “Lighad”, describing the act as belittling a Quranic verse, a matter that should not be taken lightly.
Earlier, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan stressed that the sanctity of the Quran as the primary source of Islamic teachings must always be respected and preserved.
He said any act of ridiculing or insulting the sacred words of the Quran was irresponsible and could offend the sensitivities of Muslims. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak longhouse fire leaves 25 people homeless in Ulu Tinjar
Article:
MIRI, Oct 11 — Three units of a longhouse at Rumah Wani in Ulu Tinjar were completely destroyed in a fire this morning, affecting three families comprising 25 people.
The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) said it received an emergency call at 8.20am, prompting firefighters from the Lopeng and Batu Niah fire stations to respond to the incident along Jalan Sungai Lansat.
The team arrived at the scene at 11.05am after travelling 135km to reach the longhouse.
“The fire involved three units of a longhouse built with non-permanent materials, namely units four, five and six, covering an estimated area of 54 by 100 feet.
“All three units were completely destroyed,” Bomba said in a statement.
The three affected families comprised five, 10 and 10 members respectively. No casualties were reported.
The operation was led by PBK I Abdul Rahman Rosliee, with 11 firefighters from both stations deployed to the scene. They were supported by two Fire Rescue Tenders (FRTs) and a four-wheel-drive vehicle.
The fire was brought under control at 11.20am, and the operation ended at 12.14pm after firefighters completed overhaul work to ensure no remaining hotspots could reignite the fire.
Police and Sarawak Energy personnel were also present at the scene. — The Borneo Post

Title: Melaka polls: Pakatan to unveil candidates on Oct 18, says Anwar’s aide
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Oct 11 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) will announce its candidates for the Melaka state election on October 18, with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expected to personally unveil the line-up, said his political secretary Datuk Azman Abidin.
Azman said the venue for the announcement would be announced at a later date.
“The location of the announcement will be announced later,” he told reporters after attending the ‘Jalinan Madani Rider Jelajah Melaka’ programme, which was also attended by Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abd Halim, here today.
On speculation that he would contest the Paya Rumput seat in the election, Azman said he would leave the matter to the party leadership.
He said PKR was targeting seven or eight seats in the election, including Machap Jaya and Rembia.
The Election Commission (EC) has set October 31 for nominations, November 10 for early voting and November 14 for polling, following the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly on September 23.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Schools in Melaka, N. Sembilan, Pahang, Putrajaya and parts of KL, Selangor to reopen tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang and Putrajaya, as well as several areas in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor, will resume normal operations tomorrow.
In KUALA LUMPUR, the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Education Department said MOE educational institutions under the Sentul and Keramat District Education Offices (PPDs) would reopen tomorrow, following a decline in Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the areas for three consecutive days.
“The latest reading was at a moderate level, with an API of 84 recorded at the CA15W Batu Muda station as of 2pm today. As such, the implementation of Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) and the Work From Home (WFH) directive for these areas has been terminated,” JPWPKL said in a statement.
However, JPWPKL said schools under the Bangsar/Pudu PPD would remain closed until further notice, as air quality remained at an unhealthy level, with an API reading of 152 recorded at the CA16W Cheras station during the same period.
It said that to ensure continuity of teaching and learning, PdPR and the WFH directive for teachers and Implementing Group Staff (AKP) under the Bangsar/Pudu PPD would continue.
In SELANGOR, the Selangor Education Department (JPNS) said all schools under the administration of the Hulu Langat, Gombak and Petaling Perdana PPDs would remain closed based on the latest API readings.
In a statement, JPNS also said all schools in other districts in the state would operate as usual tomorrow.
“Teachers and parents are advised to follow official updates from the authorities on developments in air quality and relevant school operation directives.
“Further information on school operations and reopening will be announced through the official channels of the MOE and JPNS,” the statement said.
In MELAKA, schools will resume normal operations tomorrow, as air quality readings remained at moderate levels below 100, according to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) as of 2pm, with Alor Gajah recording 91, Bukit Rambai 94 and Bandaraya Melaka 96.
In NEGERI SEMBILAN, the Negeri Sembilan Education Department also said all MOE educational institutions would operate as usual tomorrow based on the latest air quality monitoring.
It also advised students experiencing respiratory symptoms or those in high-risk groups to wear face masks as a precautionary measure.
In PAHANG, the Pahang Education Department also said all schools in the state would operate as usual tomorrow, with the haze situation and API readings being continuously monitored from time to time through the respective PPDs.
In PUTRAJAYA, the Putrajaya Federal Territory Education Department (JPWPP) said all schools under its administration would operate as usual tomorrow, following API readings remaining below the 150 threshold.
According to JPWPP, analysis of API readings showed a consistent decline over the past three days, with the API standing at 70 as of 2pm today. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Air quality in Kuching, Miri improves to moderate levels, says DOE
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 11 — Air quality in Kuching and Miri has improved but remains in the moderate category, according to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index of Malaysia (APIMS) portal on Sunday.
Kuching’s Air Pollutant Index (API) reading last recorded an unhealthy level at 2am today, at 111, before dropping to 99 at 3am.
The reading subsequently declined from 153 at 3pm yesterday (Oct 10) to 85 at 3pm today, placing Kuching in the moderate category.
In Miri, the API reading last recorded an unhealthy level at noon today, at 104, before falling to 99 at 1pm.
Miri’s API reading had remained in the moderate category from 3pm yesterday until 11am today, when it rose to 101 before reaching 104 at noon.
As of 3pm today, all air quality monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded API readings within the moderate category.
The readings were Limbang (84), ILP Miri (80), Miri (98), Samalaju (96), Bintulu (94), Mukah (79), Kapit (66), Sibu (87), Sarikei (84), Sri Aman (61), Samarahan (74), Kuching (85) and IPD Serian (70). — The Borneo Post

Title: Digital tools, AI can preserve Dusun language for future generations, says Sabah deputy CM
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 11 — Digital technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), has the potential to become a crucial medium in efforts to preserve the Dusun language, ensuring that this community’s heritage continues to be learned, used, and inherited by future generations.
Sabah Deputy Chief Minister I Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam said that modern technology can be leveraged through the development of digital dictionaries, recordings of Dusun speech, podcast production, and the creation of online learning materials.
He noted that these efforts need to be strengthened through the involvement of the younger generation, educational institutions, and local communities so that the Dusun language remains relevant and continues to be used in daily life.
“When a language is used less and less, we are actually at risk of losing a part of our own community’s identity and heritage,” he said.
“The question is, in the next 50 years, will our children and grandchildren still be able to speak their mother tongue and understand the history, customs, and culture that form the foundation of their identity?” he said in a statement today.
Joachim, who is also Sabah’s Minister of Works and Utilities, made these remarks while speaking at the closing ceremony of the Ranau Dusun Language and Culture Festival in Ranau yesterday.
He also encouraged schools, colleges, and universities to establish collaborations with cultural organisations and local communities to collect and document materials related to Dusun history, language, and culture for use in education and research.
He stated that the responsibility of ensuring the survival of the Dusun language does not rest solely on certain parties; rather, it requires the commitment of the entire community, especially parents and the younger generation, to continue practicing the use of their mother tongue.
Consequently, he hopes that efforts to elevate the Dusun language will not stop after the conclusion of the festival, but will instead be continued through education, documentation, research, and the active use of the language in community life. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Socso offers up to RM150 tax relief for Lindung 24 Jam, Lindung Kendiri contributors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Contributors who remain under the Lindung 24 Jam Scheme, as well as those making mandatory contributions to the Lindung Kendiri Scheme, will be eligible for additional tax relief of up to RM150 under Budget 2027.
The Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), in a statement today, said the initiative is expected to benefit more than 8.5 million Lindung 24 Jam contributors and 1.7 million Lindung Kendiri contributors.
“The Lindung 24 Jam Scheme recorded 10,424 claims in its first four months of implementation, averaging 85 claims a day and highlighting the need for protection against risks that extend beyond working hours.
“It is hoped that the incentive will encourage more people to obtain coverage under Lindung 24 Jam, including those who had previously opted out but may now rejoin, while also increasing participation in Lindung Kendiri,” it said.
Under Budget 2027, e-hailing and p-hailing workers will also receive a 35 per cent matching contribution from Perkeso, with the rate increasing to 50 per cent if platform companies also contribute towards their social security payments.
A 70 per cent matching contribution incentive will also be extended to more than 200,000 self-employed individuals across 17 non-mandatory sectors to ease their contribution burden and broaden access to social security protection.
“Perkeso welcomes the initiative and will ensure that all operational and system preparations are in place to enable self-employed individuals to contribute to Lindung Kendiri and benefit from the matching contribution incentive,” it said.
Meanwhile, more than 40,000 religious functionaries, including imams, bilals, tok siak, noja and marbut and takmir teachers, will also benefit from Perkeso coverage funded by Lembaga Tabung Haji.
Perkeso will also provide health screening vouchers to commercial heavy vehicle drivers aged 40 and above under the Safe and Healthy Driver (PSS) programme to facilitate the early detection of health issues and reduce driving-related risks. — Bernama
Note: Perkeso is also known as Socso, the English acronym for Social Security Organisation.

Title: Budget 2027: Nadma to use RM260m allocation for disaster relief centres, equipment, says Zahid
Article:
IPOH, Oct 11 — The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) will prioritise the RM260 million allocated under Budget 2027 for establishing more Permanent Disaster Relief Centres (PPKBs) and procuring disaster preparedness assets and equipment, said Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
The deputy prime minister said the move would enable Nadma to assist frontline agencies in enhancing their operational capabilities, particularly in dealing with disasters such as floods.
“We want to establish two permanent disaster relief centres in each state. Insya-Allah, with the additional allocation next year, we will add more according to requirements,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee chairman, said this at a press conference after launching the 2026 National Preparedness Month (BKN) at the Ipoh Convention Centre here today.
He said the target of establishing two PPKBs in each state would focus on hotspot areas that frequently experience floods and require the evacuation of large numbers of victims.
On July 6, Deputy Digital Minister Datuk Wilson Ugak Kumbong, representing the Rural and Regional Development Ministry, said during a Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat that 15 PPKBs involving nine states were expected to begin operations in stages from this year as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s disaster management system.
Of the total, one PPKB each in Johor and Pahang has been fully completed, nine are under construction, while the remaining four are at the procurement and planning stages.
Ahmad Zahid also said the allocation would also be used to procure disaster preparedness assets and equipment, such as boats and water pumps, for relevant agencies.
He said the rate of assistance for repairing homes affected by disasters had also been increased from RM5,000 to RM10,000 per family to help victims repair their homes and rebuild their lives after a disaster.
“In addition, aid management has also been improved, with Bantuan Wang Ihsan being distributed to victims while they are at Temporary Evacuation Centres, before they return to their respective homes, to expedite assistance to affected families,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Health Ministry steps up efforts to recruit, retain nurses amid overseas migration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is expediting nurse recruitment and strengthening efforts to retain those already in service through improved welfare support and career advancement opportunities to address the migration of nurses abroad.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the measures include salary adjustments under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), as well as incentives and allowances for eligible personnel, including an increase in the Post-Basic Incentive from RM100 to RM200 a month.
“The MOH’s priority is to ensure that public nursing services remain competitive while safeguarding the welfare of nurses,” he told reporters after launching the National Liver Health Initiative Roadmap 2026-2030 at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, here today.
Dzulkefly said other measures included maintaining the 42-hour working week for nurses on shift duty, expanding training and promotion opportunities, and offering greater flexibility in placements through a mutual exchange system.
He said nurses were among those who benefited most from the mutual exchange system, with recruitment also being expedited to fill existing vacancies.
Dzulkefly said the MOH no longer recruited nurses on a contract basis, with all new recruits offered permanent appointments.
Meanwhile, he said the MOH was working with the Ministry of Finance to expedite the absorption of contract pharmacists into permanent positions.
As of July, 3,545 contract pharmacists were still serving with the MOH, while another 115 were on the reserve list or awaiting permanent appointments, he said.
Dzulkefly expressed hope that the appointment process could be expedited to enable these pharmacists to enter the permanent service. — Bernama

Title: Pakatan targets Tampin parliamentary seat comeback in next GE
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is aiming to reclaim the Tampin parliamentary seat at the next general election, with its election machinery urged to strengthen its efforts and engage voters from now.
Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) deputy president Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun said all parties must work harder to restore public confidence and demonstrate PH’s capabilities through its administrative performance and service to the community, Kosmo! Online reported today.
Aminuddin, who is also Negeri Sembilan PH chairman, said winning back Tampin should be one of the coalition’s main priorities as it prepares for the general election, which is expected to be held in October or November next year.
“Make sure we win. We want to restore our dignity in Tampin. Everyone must work and show the people what we have accomplished.
“The people can see who is capable of working and who merely talks big but cannot fulfil their responsibilities,” he said in his speech at the DAP Negeri Sembilan convention in Seremban today.
Commenting on PH’s defeat in the previous Negeri Sembilan state election, Aminuddin said the experience should serve as a lesson, particularly in addressing racial sentiments which were alleged to have divided support for the coalition.
He said a campaign against DAP that played on Malay sentiment appeared to have affected voter support, including in Malay-majority constituencies where PH’s Malay candidates also lost.

Title: Selangor career carnival offers 3,568 jobs for vulnerable groups
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 11 — The Selangor government has expanded job opportunities for vulnerable groups through the Selangor JobCare Istimewa Career Carnival 2026, which offers 3,568 vacancies.
State Human Resources and Poverty Eradication Committee chairman V. Papparaidu said the state government was aware of the challenges faced by these groups in entering the job market, particularly persons with disabilities (OKU), Orang Asli, military veterans and senior citizens.
He said the carnival, involving 40 employers from various sectors, provided more opportunities for jobseekers to find roles matching their qualifications, skills and experience.
“The 3,568 positions available include 1,603 vacancies for Orang Asli, veterans (1,333), OKU (472) and senior citizens (160).
“Of the total, 2,854 vacancies or 80 per cent are in Selangor, while the remainder involve placements in other states,” he said.
He said this in his speech at the carnival’s opening ceremony, officiated by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari at the Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) Convention Centre here today.
Papparaidu said employment opportunities for the Orang Asli community would help boost household income and elevate their socio-economic status, including that of the younger generation.
“For veterans, their experience, discipline and skills gained throughout their service are valuable assets that can be tapped by both the public and private sectors.
“Persons with disabilities are capable of being productive employees and contributing to organisations, while senior citizens can continue to contribute to society and the economy,” he said.
He said the one-day carnival offered career opportunities with salaries ranging between RM5,000 and RM12,999, including positions in management, technical and engineering fields.
“Therefore, human capital development remains a continuous priority, and we must ensure that Selangor residents are not only ready for the job market but also able to increase their income and build sustainable careers,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Disaster preparedness key to reducing property losses
Article:
IPOH, Oct 11 — Preparedness in disaster management helps reduce property losses, including damage to public assets and infrastructure, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said that losses due to disasters in the country last year reached RM636.9 million, including RM380.2 million involving public assets and infrastructure.
“This figure was lower than the RM933.4 million in 2024. That is why preparedness must protect two important values, namely the value of life and economic value. Yes, we want to save lives, while also protecting homes, taking care of people’s livelihoods and preserving the fruits of the people’s hard work.
“This is where the early warning system comes in. These are awareness programmes that we must collectively translate into action. We want to raise public awareness of the importance of National Preparedness Month (BKN) in building the capacity to address potential risks before disaster strikes,” said Ahmad Zahid, who also chairs the Central Disaster Management Committee.
He said this when officiating at the launch of BKN 2026 at the Ipoh Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) director-general Datuk Seri Meor Ismail Meor Akim.
Ahmad Zahid said rescue teams would be mobilised whenever a disaster occurred, while the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) provided early warning systems to identify hotspots expected to experience floods and other disaster risks.
“The MetMalaysia director-general will input data into the system and notify Nadma, and me specifically, so that we can inform potential victims to evacuate and be prepared at least three days before a disaster strikes.
“However, the ability to respond efficiently after a disaster must be accompanied by a strong commitment to reducing risks before they occur. Our success is also be measured by how effectively we protect the public and reduce the risks faced by those who may be affected,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said disaster risk reduction should begin at the land-use planning and urban development stages, including identifying areas at risk of landslides and taking early action.
In addition, he said river management and the monitoring of high-risk areas are crucial for mitigating the impact of disasters.
He said early warning must be timely, easily understood and followed by actions to save lives during disasters, including giving families sufficient time to evacuate before water levels rise and helping the elderly and children reach safety, with effective communication being a key factor.
Ahmad Zahid also urged every state to translate the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2030 into action plans tailored to local risks, with clearly defined agency responsibilities and implementation targets to ensure comprehensive protection for the people.
“We have managed to develop the Cell Broadcast System through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), which is now in its final stage. The system does not merely monitor TikTok and other online posts; it also allows alerts to be sent directly to mobile phones in at-risk areas without interfering with or using personal data,” he added.
He said field operations were also supported by volunteers, with nearly 30,000 volunteers from 45 agencies across 14 states participating in more than 1,000 disaster relief missions over the past 10 months.
“We adhere to the two Cs: communication and coordination, with the two Cs meaning information must be conveyed clearly and on time.
“Actions must also be coordinated so that the people know what needs to be done, the committee knows how to provide assistance and agencies can act without delay.. this is the shift I want to see resulting from this National Preparedness Month,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Schools in Perak, Negeri Sembilan to reopen tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Schools in three Perak districts and educational institutions across Negeri Sembilan will resume normal operations tomorrow, following reviews of air quality and prevailing conditions.
Perak Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said schools in Kinta Utara, Kinta Selatan and Kuala Kangsar could reopen after Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at all monitoring stations in the state remained below 150 as of 2pm today, according to a report by national news agency Bernama.
The schools had been closed last Friday after unhealthy air quality was recorded in the affected areas.
Khairudin said conditions had improved compared with the previous two or three days, adding that he hoped the weather would remain favourable for pupils to continue their lessons without disruption.
He also cautioned the public against circulating false information about school closures, saying official announcements would be issued only by the state Education Department.
In Negeri Sembilan, the state Education Department said all educational institutions under its jurisdiction would operate as usual on Monday after reviewing the latest API readings and current conditions.
The department advised schools to keep track of air quality and follow the relevant guidelines to safeguard pupils and staff.
It also recommended that pupils wear face masks as a precaution, particularly those with respiratory symptoms or who fall into high-risk groups.
Both departments said they would continue monitoring the situation and communicate any changes through their official channels.

Title: Melaka schools reopen tomorrow as API readings dip below 100, says state exco
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 11 — All educational institutions under the Ministry of Education in Melaka will reopen tomorrow (October 12) after the Air Pollutant Index (API) recorded moderate readings below 100.
State Education, Higher Education and Religious Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Rahmad Mariman said the decision took into account the latest air quality developments and prioritised the education, safety and well-being of students, teachers and all members of educational institutions.
“Accordingly, administrators of educational institutions are urged to take appropriate measures to ensure the smooth operation of their respective institutions and to comply with current directives and guidelines set by the Ministry of Education and relevant authorities.
“Parents and guardians are also advised to continue monitoring their children’s health and to seek treatment if they experience symptoms related to air pollution,” he said in a statement here today.
He said any changes to operating directives would be communicated through the official channels of the Melaka State Education Department (JPN).
JPN Melaka expressed its appreciation for the concern shown by all parties in ensuring the continuity of education and safeguarding the entire educational community in Melaka.
Based on data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Melaka recorded moderate API readings as of 2 pm today: Alor Gajah (91), Bukit Rambai (94) and Bandaraya Melaka (96). — Bernama

Title: Haze: Malaysia still awaiting Indonesia’s response to firefighting aid offer, says DPM Zahid
Article:
IPOH, Oct 11 — Malaysia is still awaiting a response from Indonesia on its offer to help put out forest and land fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan that have caused transboundary haze, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said that during a visit to Jakarta last month, he had met Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and a representative of the Vice-President to discuss the offer of assistance.
“The National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and the Foreign Ministry have also written to their respective counterparts, but there has been no response yet.
“We take a positive view that perhaps they do not require our assistance. We remain optimistic and assume the best,” he told reporters after officiating the launch of National Preparedness Month (BKN) 2026 at the Ipoh Convention Centre here today.
In his speech, Ahmad Zahid, who is also chairman of the National Disaster Management Committee, said Malaysia had offered a firefighting aircraft, three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel to assist with firefighting operations in Indonesia.
Meanwhile, he said the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) not only assisted in managing disasters domestically but was also always ready to provide aid to other countries affected by disasters.
He said the team had also been deployed to Nepal to help locate 55 Malaysians who remained uncontactable following a disaster there, including by sending DNA samples to assist in the identification process.
“So far, we have not found any remains to be brought back to Malaysia. We are still waiting, and I would like to congratulate the SMART team,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid also expressed pride in SMART’s recognition as the second-best rescue team in Asia after Japan.
He said SMART had also retained its international Heavy Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) classification after undergoing a 36-hour assessment involving 173 criteria. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Digital Ministry targets 200,000 AI-skilled individuals in push for AI Nation by 2030
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 11 — The Ministry of Digital is intensifying efforts to strengthen the nation’s digital ecosystem, empower local tech talent and build a future-ready workforce under Budget 2027, as part of Malaysia’s broader ambition to become an AI Nation by 2030.
In a statement today, the Ministry said these efforts include producing 200,000 AI-skilled individuals by strengthening AI Malaysia Bhd, with a focus on developing high-skilled talent, digital infrastructure and efficient, secure and ethical AI governance.
“The Fifth Madani Budget, themed “Menggapai Di Langit, Mengakar Di Bumi” (Reaching for the Skies, While Anchored on Our Values), tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim last Friday, reflects the government’s bold commitment to driving the nation’s digital transformation towards an AI Nation, anchored in the inclusive Malaysia Digital framework,” the statement read.
The Ministry of Digital also announced that under Budget 2027, funds from the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) will be channelled to help 4,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) adopt AI technology and automate their operations, in support of local business growth.
The initiative, according to the statement, also includes training and certification for 5,000 AI professionals, aimed at upgrading the skills and capabilities of the sector’s workforce.
In a bid to attract local and international talent, the government also announced a two-year extension of the DE Rantau Nomad Pass for existing holders who have reached the maximum two-year limit, allowing them to continue living and working remotely in Malaysia.
The Ministry said the inclusive digitalisation agenda will also be extended to more than 300 pondok schools nationwide through a collaboration between the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia and MDEC, including providing devices and digital skills training for teachers and students.
The statement added that an extra 100,000 free subscriptions to popular AI applications, including ChatGPT, will broaden public access to the technology, empowering digital skills and human capital, particularly among youths.
It said the Digital Rakyat Platform offers Malaysians free access to over 16,000 digital courses and Professional Certificates in partnership with Coursera.
“These measures translate the philosophy of ‘Reaching for the Skies, While Anchored on Our Values’ into action, positioning Malaysia on the global high-tech stage while ensuring that no group is left behind in the digital development agenda.
“The Ministry of Digital welcomes the commitment shown in this budget and stands ready to mobilise every capability to accelerate the nation’s digital transformation, thereby propelling Malaysia towards becoming a resilient AI Nation by 2030,” the statement read.
Budget 2027 provides a government allocation of RM459.8 billion, complemented by RM25 billion in investment from government-linked investment companies, RM11 billion in public-private investment and RM14.2 billion from Federal Statutory Bodies and Minister of Finance (Incorporated) companies, bringing the total to RM510 billion and continuing an expansionary fiscal policy. — Bernama

Title: Defence Ministry to use idle military land for food security, veteran welfare, says Khaled Nordin
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Oct 11 — The Ministry of Defence (Mindef) is taking a proactive approach to using undeveloped Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) land to support the national food security agenda and boost veterans’ socioeconomic welfare.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the JanaVeteran Programme, in collaboration with Boustead Plantations (BPlant), could carry out this programme.
“We do not want Mindef land with no allocation or development plans to sit idle. Some plots have gone untouched for 10 to 15 years simply because there are no plans yet.
“So we want BPlant to help the country strengthen food security,” he said at a press conference after launching JanaKomuniti at Felda Air Tawar 3 here today.
He said the move would provide job opportunities and income for military veterans while keeping them productive.
“Every year, 5,000 military personnel retire, so one approach is to introduce any veteran interested in agriculture to the programme,” he said.
Mohamad said food security must be given serious attention, as supply shortages or rising food costs could escalate into a national security threat.
He said the situation was similar to haze, which, if prolonged and widespread, could become a non-traditional security threat.
He said the JanaVeteran pilot project began with KayTi ginger cultivation at Ladang Telok Sengat here, and its model guarantees a market for participants, with BPlant buying the produce.
Meanwhile, Mohamed Khaled, who is also the Kota Tinggi MP, aims to make the district the country’s main producer of KayTi ginger, carried out with BPlant through the JanaKomuniti Programme at Felda Air Tawar 3 and Felda Air Tawar 2.
“When this programme succeeds, we will ultimately have a recognisable KayTi ginger product, with Kota Tinggi becoming the nation’s food valley through the cultivation of this ginger,” he said.
The JanaKomuniti Programme is one of BPlant’s corporate social responsibility initiatives, supported by the Kota Tinggi Parliamentary Office, through a clustered fertigation ginger farming project. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia in high-level contact over haze as Jakarta deploys 60,000 to fight fires, says Indonesian minister
Article:
JAKARTA, Oct 11 — Indonesia and Malaysia have maintained high-level diplomatic communication over transboundary haze caused by forest and land fires, following a telephone conversation between their leaders amid concerns over worsening air pollution.
Indonesian Foreign Minister Arrmanatha Nasir said he had spoken to his Malaysian counterpart Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, to explain Indonesia’s firefighting efforts.
“We have deployed more than 60,000 personnel. This is indeed a challenge because weather conditions are currently not in our favour, but we hope the situation will ease soon as rainfall is expected,” he told reporters.
Arrmanatha was responding to questions about Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s statement on Thursday that he had contacted Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto over the haze situation.
Anwar also said Malaysia was ready to assist Indonesia in tackling the fires and had instructed the Foreign Minister to contact the Asean Secretariat to seek a meeting of regional environment ministers to coordinate efforts to combat transboundary haze.
Meanwhile, Indonesia’s Forestry Ministry reported a sharp increase in hotspots nationwide, to 793 as of 9.10 pm local time on Saturday, up from 437 the previous day. The six priority provinces accounted for 421 hotspots, up from 270 a day earlier.
According to the ministry’s monitoring system, Central Kalimantan recorded the highest number, at 288, followed by South Sumatra (60), West Kalimantan (44), South Kalimantan (28) and Jambi (one), while Riau recorded none.
“Today’s increase serves as a reminder that vigilance must not depend on trends over just one or two days,” the ministry said in a video update posted on its official Instagram account.
The ministry said air quality monitoring based on PM2.5 concentrations continued to show unhealthy to very unhealthy conditions in several areas, with pockets of hazardous pollution detected in parts of Kalimantan, Sumatra and Papua.
It added that 61 aircraft remained on standby, comprising 44 for water-bombing operations and 17 for aerial patrols and weather-modification operations, supported by ground firefighting teams. — Bernama

Title: Claims that Tabung Haji depositors’ money funded Socso contributions for religious workers untrue, says Zulkifli Hasan
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 11 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan said that Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) depositors’ savings were not used to pay Social Security Organisation (Socso) contributions for 40,000 mosque personnel and takmir teachers nationwide.
He said a special government allocation fully funded the contributions, channeled through TH as the implementing agency.
Zulkifli said the government’s decision to fully fund the contributions recognises religious personnel’s service and helps safeguard their welfare, social protection and wellbeing.
“Any claims or assumptions that pilgrims’ savings have been used are entirely untrue and speculative,” he said in a statement today.
The beneficiaries include imams, bilals, mosque caretakers and takmir teachers serving Muslim communities nationwide.
Zulkifli said the government is committed to ensuring that TH upholds integrity in managing its trust funds and maintains transparent corporate governance in accordance with Syariah principles.
He said the government will continue to prioritise the welfare of mosque personnel and takmir teachers to safeguard religious institutions and support the development of the Muslim community in Malaysia. — Bernama
Note: Socso is also known as Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial (Perkeso) in Malay.

Title: ‘Negeri Sembilan crisis is not DAP’s fault’, says Anthony Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — DAP has stressed that it is not responsible for the ongoing political crisis in Negeri Sembilan.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook said it was unfair to continue blaming the party for the crisis when it was no longer part of the state government, according to a report by
Sinar Harian
today.
“What is happening today is certainly not caused by us. During the Negeri Sembilan state election campaign, they tried to link DAP to the crisis, claiming that we were responsible for what was happening in the state.
“Today, we are already outside the government. So they can no longer blame us or use DAP as an excuse,” he told reporters on the sidelines of the 24th DAP Negeri Sembilan annual convention here on Sunday.
The Seremban MP also said the turmoil in the state appeared to have no end in sight as it involved various factors, including the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
He said the situation was compounded by Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim’s refusal to submit a new list of state executive councillors, as instructed by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
“There is actually no reason why they (Barisan Nasional) cannot continue governing as usual, because Tuanku Muhriz has asked the menteri besar to submit the names of the new state executive councillors.
“So there is actually no problem. They can choose other people, but the next move is up to them,” he said.
However, Anthony said it was unusual for a state government to have only a menteri besar without a team of executive councillors.
He added that the situation would inevitably disrupt the smooth running of the state administration, as many decisions and administrative matters required approval from the State Executive Council.
“As far as BN’s political manoeuvring is concerned, that is up to them. They have a majority in the state legislative assembly.
“But we have never been involved in any effort of that kind, such as a vote of no confidence against the menteri besar. As I have said, we are focused on our work, and most importantly, I have reminded our elected representatives to stay focused on their duties,” he said when asked about the possibility of BN moving a vote of no confidence against Ismail.
Asked whether the crisis could drag on for a longer period, Anthony said he was unsure but that DAP was prepared for any eventuality.

Title: JPJ suspends Chery Omoda 5 approval, new registrations after rear axle incident in Johor Bahru
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) has temporarily suspended the Vehicle Type Approval (VTA) for the affected Chery Omoda 5 model and variants following a safety concern arising from an incident that went viral in Johor Bahru last week.
JPJ director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the action also involved a suspension of new registrations for the vehicles until technical investigations were completed and the safety risks identified, Kosmo! Online reported today.
He said the move was an early precautionary measure to safeguard road users.
“JPJ views seriously the viral incident involving a Chery Omoda 5 in Johor Bahru last week, which raised public concerns over the safety of the vehicle.
“As an initial precaution, JPJ will temporarily suspend the relevant VTA, thereby halting new registrations of the Chery Omoda 5 until technical investigations are completed and safety risks identified,” he said in a statement today.
He said the suspension would be targeted at the models and variants potentially involved.
At the same time, Chery Malaysia has been instructed to identify all potentially affected vehicles based on component numbers, production batches, vehicle identification numbers (VINs) and other relevant technical parameters.
He said a recall must be carried out for all vehicles identified as being at risk to allow the necessary inspections and corrective action to be undertaken.
“JPJ is also conducting a technical audit of the Chery Omoda 5 manufacturing and assembly processes, as well as the supplier of the relevant axle components.
“The audit covers compliance with good manufacturing practices (GMP), quality control systems, weld joint inspection procedures and the safety standards of the components used,” he said.
He added that manufacturers were responsible for ensuring every vehicle sold met the stipulated safety standards and technical requirements.
“The suspension will only be lifted after all corrective and preventive measures have been fully implemented and JPJ has provided technical confirmation that all safety risks have been adequately addressed,” he said.
Earlier, an incident involving the rear axle of a Chery vehicle coming off in Tebrau, Johor Bahru, went viral on social media.

Title: Budget 2027: PTPTN offers 10pc discount to borrowers with no arrears who make regular repayments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers with no arrears who make regular repayments will enjoy a 10 per cent discount from 2027.
PTPTN chairman Datuk Seri Norliza Abdul Rahim said the incentive was a form of recognition for borrowers who demonstrated discipline in fulfilling their loan repayment obligations.
“The initiative, which will be implemented in 2027, aims to encourage consistent repayments and reduce the risk of loan arrears,” she said in a statement today.
She said the government has announced an initiative to defer PTPTN loan repayments in 2027, which would benefit more than 400,000 borrowers, as well as a minimum monthly repayment of RM50 for low-income borrowers.
Norliza said implementation of the initiative would be subject to income verification through cross-checks with the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia.
“This reflects the government’s concern in ensuring that repayment commitments can be aligned with borrowers’ financial capacity,” she said.
She said another initiative involved granting tax deductions to employers who repaid PTPTN loans on behalf of their employees, covering payments made from January 2027 to December 2028.
She said the initiative would encourage employers to help ease their employees’ debt burden while safeguarding their welfare.
“As an agency under the Ministry of Higher Education, PTPTN remains committed to realising the government’s goals and aspirations under Budget 2027 by expanding access to more inclusive education, improving borrowers’ well-being and ensuring the sustainability of education financing funds,” she said.
She said this is to ensure that more young people have the opportunity to build their future through higher education.
On Friday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, when tabling Budget 2027, announced that the government agreed to defer PTPTN loan repayments for borrowers earning less than RM2,500 a month.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said borrowers earning between RM2,500 and RM3,000 a month would only be required to make minimum repayments of RM50. — Bernama

Title: LCS 1 completion not tied to RCI, shipbuilder told to speed up work, says defence minister
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Oct 11 — The establishment of a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) to investigate delays in the Royal Malaysian Navy’s (RMN) Littoral Combat Ship (LCS) project is not a determining factor in ensuring the prompt completion of the country’s defence asset.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the shipbuilder had been instructed to expedite work and ensure that further delays did not occur.
“The completion of LCS 1 is a separate matter and does not depend on the RCI. Otherwise, the ship would still not be completed. That is why we have asked the shipbuilder to speed up the work and ensure there are no further delays,” he told reporters.
He was speaking after attending the first harvest of the KayTi JanaVeteran Ginger Project and the launch of JanaKomuniti at Telok Sengat Farm and Felda Air Tawar here today.
Mohamed Khaled was responding to a call by Pasir Gudang MP Hasan Karim for the investigation into the LCS project to be expedited and not made dependent on the RCI, following the Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026, which found that the project was 7.55 per cent behind schedule as of June 25.
Lumut Naval Shipyard (LUNAS), the company responsible for building Malaysia’s first LCS, has set April 2027 as the revised delivery date for LCS 1 to the Defence Ministry (Mindef) under Phase 1.
The new date was set after LUNAS informed the ministry that it could not provide a commitment or guarantee that the ship would be delivered by December this year.
On the investigation, Mohamed Khaled said the matter should be left to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the relevant authorities.
He also referred to court action previously taken against a former Navy chief who had also served as managing director of Boustead Naval Shipyard Sdn Bhd (BNS) in connection with the LCS project.
Meanwhile, Mohamed Khaled said the government was in negotiations with several shortlisted countries to procure a surface-to-surface missile system for LCS 1 to replace Norway’s Naval Strike Missile (NSM).
He said the procurement would not depend on the Budget 2027 allocation, as the ministry wanted to ensure that LCS 1 would not take too long to be fully equipped.
He said the ship was currently equipped with surface-to-air missiles, anti-submarine warfare capabilities and an electronic jamming system, with surface-to-surface missiles being the remaining capability yet to be installed. — Bernama
